whatChanged: NEW: BASF has made a non-binding approach for a voluntary public takeover of Evonik and confirmed exploratory talks with Evonik and its 43.8% holder RAG-Stiftung; Evonik says no talks are under way. Evonik closed up 7.2% (evk-basf-acquisition)

NEW: Harworth's board now recommends Peel's increased 187p-a-share best-and-final cash offer, valuing the developer at £631.7m, a 30.2% premium to the undisturbed price. Peel is buying 72m shares to take a majority on 29 September (hwg-peel-acquisition)

NEW: Anthropic will pay Akamai $11.6bn over seven years for cloud capacity, with a $9bn option and a warrant for about 5% of Akamai. Akamai is raising 2026 capex by about $1.7bn and its shares rose about 20% after hours (akam-anthropic-cloud-deal)

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsors, strategics and now insiders keep taking listed businesses off public markets, and the spread between what the public market pays and what private capital will pay is the whole story. The newest case is also the most conflicted: Priority Technology's chairman and CEO Thomas Priore is buying the stock his group does not own at $8.05 a share, a $1.6bn enterprise value backed by a Searchlight Capital Partners equity commitment -- a special committee dragged him more than 30% above his opening $6.00-$6.15 range, which is the clearest evidence yet that the opening bid in an insider buyout is a floor, not a valuation (prth-priore-searchlight-take-private). Third-party sponsors show the full range in a fortnight: Sequence Holdings and Michael Dell's DFO Management are paying $32.50 a share for Baldwin, an 88% premium to its unaffected June price at a $7.7bn enterprise value, while H.I.G. is taking MISTRAS at $20.35 for an $866m enterprise value and a premium of just 8% to the 30-day VWAP, with 31% of the register locked into support agreements and a go-shop to 27 October the only route to more (bwin-sequence-dfo-take-private, mg-hig-take-private). The contested approaches are still unresolved: Uber's EUR41.50-a-share tender for Delivery Hero runs to November on a minimum of 50% plus one share (dher-uber-takeover-offer), and Curaleaf's hostile tender for Aurora Cannabis runs to 1 December against a board circular telling holders to reject, with Aurora now asking the Alberta Securities Commission to force a corrected circular -- pro forma financials, a French-language Quebec notice and the 105-day minimum deposit period, without which the bid is not a 'permitted bid' under Aurora's rights plan (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid). Two are effectively done: L'imad has met every condition of its AED6.25-a-share offer for AD Ports and will own more than 98.5% and delist it once settlement completes by 9 October (adports-limad-takeover-bid), and Copart is tendering $10.50 a share for ACV Auctions to 30 September, a 45% premium that takes a listed digital-auction rival off the market (cprt-acv-acquisition). The newest is a UK property developer: Harworth's board, having resisted, now recommends Peel's increased 187p-a-share best-and-final cash offer, a 30% premium to the undisturbed price that values it at £631.7m, and Peel expects to hold a majority once a 72m-share purchase settles on 29 September (hwg-peel-acquisition).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps flowing to the physical layer of AI compute, and the bottleneck keeps moving down the stack to power and silicon supply. Getting power onto a site is the scarcest input, and Amazon has contracted the generators themselves, committing $2.4bn across 2027-28 and up to $8bn over the life of a backup-power agreement with Generac -- a company whose franchise was suburban home standby until this deal made hyperscaler capex its swing factor (gnrc-amazon-generator-supply). The pull now reaches the regulated utilities and the politics around them: NextEra's $67bn all-stock purchase of Dominion, the largest regulated utility deal ever announced, is being fought in Virginia over exactly who pays for data-center load growth, with the September concession package funding four years of residential bill credits by redirecting credits that would otherwise have gone to data centers -- a package Virginia's attorney general now argues is a new deal that should restart the 180-day review clock and push the hearing to January (nee-dominion-acquisition). At the silicon layer the buildout has produced its first credible second source for inference: AWS may take up to $60bn of Qualcomm custom inference chips and 1.6Tbps optical interconnect over ten years (qcom-aws-ai-chip-deal). The pull has now reached CDN and edge-compute providers: Anthropic will pay Akamai $11.6bn over seven years, with an option for $9bn more, for CPU-heavy cloud capacity, and Akamai is lifting 2026 capex by about $1.7bn to build it (akam-anthropic-cloud-deal).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep being resolved by regulators, politicians and courts rather than by the parties. Paramount's $111bn purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery had cleared 68 jurisdictions and still could not close until the 12-state antitrust suit was settled on 21 September; there were no divestitures, but the price was a five-year court-enforceable behavioural package -- $1.5bn of extra domestic film spend, a 30-then-32 annual release floor with a $30m payment per film missed, a $47.5m worker fund, a five-year ban on selling the Los Angeles lots and an independent board over CBS News and CNN -- commitments that are now fixed charges on the synergy case, with closing guided to early October -- and the settlement itself is now the obstacle: at a 24 September hearing Judge Martinez-Olguin said the court 'is not a rubber stamp', admitted amicus briefs from the Block the Merger coalition, asked the parties to answer Senator Booker's objections by 28 September and deferred her ruling, putting the 30 September close at risk and the ~$7m-a-day ticking fee owed to WBD holders from 1 October in play (psky-wbd-acquisition). Kone's EUR29.4bn purchase of TK Elevator is the freshest version and the most exposed: the UK Competition and Markets Authority has begun canvassing third parties ahead of a phase 1 case while the US Department of Justice runs an in-depth review that can last a year or more, against a Q2 2027 completion target (knebv-tkelevator-acquisition). Uber-Delivery Hero shows how long the tail runs even when nobody is fighting: an agreed, board-recommended tender has now entered pre-merger review in Korea, where the regulator is examining common control of Uber's taxi-hailing arm and Baedal Minjok, one clearance among a 99-country footprint that pushes settlement into the second half of 2027 (dher-uber-takeover-offer). NextEra-Dominion is the unresolved US version: every economic term is agreed and both shareholder bases have voted, yet the deal turns on Virginia's State Corporation Commission, and the companies have already doubled residential bill relief and lifted the credit pool to $1.87bn to buy approval -- only for the state attorney general to argue that the concessions amount to an amended application that should reset the 180-day review clock and move the hearing to January (nee-dominion-acquisition). The counter-example is what a clean path looks like: Bio-Techne's US antitrust waiting period simply expired and its holders voted the Merck KGaA deal through, leaving only foreign clearances (tech-merckkgaa-acquisition); Iridium holders likewise voted 99.6% for Rocket Lab's cash-and-stock offer, though regulatory work still stretches the close to mid-2027 (irdm-rocketlab-acquisition). In Canada the Alberta Securities Commission has been drafted into the Curaleaf-Aurora fight by both sides (acb-curaleaf-takeover-bid).

themes.label: Financial firms buying platforms and product lines rather than building them
themes.note: Companies keep concluding that the capabilities the market now pays for are quicker to buy than to build, and that what they are buying is a distribution platform or a fee stream rather than assets. Grab has paid $1.49bn for 60% of Atome Financial to acquire a working BNPL, cards and digital-lending platform across five Southeast Asian markets rather than originating its own book (grab-atome-acquisition). The domestic version is Aon's $17bn all-cash purchase of USI's middle-market brokerage platform from KKR, now funded with a $13.5bn seven-part bond sale that drew about $65bn of orders -- the price of buying rather than building, written onto Aon's own balance sheet (aon-usi-acquisition).

themes.label: Hyperscalers taking warrants in the suppliers they commit to
themes.note: Amazon has now twice paid for scarce AI-infrastructure supply partly in the supplier's own equity, and in both cases the warrants vest against purchases rather than at signing, so the customer is compensated for the volume it actually delivers. Qualcomm granted Amazon warrants worth about $4bn, struck at $161.26, alongside an agreement under which AWS may buy up to $60bn of custom inference silicon and 1.6Tbps optical interconnect over ten years (qcom-aws-ai-chip-deal); Generac granted warrants over up to 1,693,745 shares at $200.93, roughly 308,000 exercisable immediately and the rest unlocking as Amazon pays for generators under a $2.4bn-committed, up-to-$8bn backup-power pact (gnrc-amazon-generator-supply). For the supplier the contract is transformative revenue bought with dilution that only bites if the volume arrives; for holders it caps the upside from the very re-rating the announcement triggers -- Generac's stock moved more than 40% on the news, most of which now accrues in part to the counterparty. The mechanism is spreading beyond hyperscalers to AI labs: Anthropic's $11.6bn Akamai cloud contract comes with a warrant over up to 7.7m as-converted Akamai shares (about 5%) at $111.33 (akam-anthropic-cloud-deal).
